title: New Sweden
capsule: New Sweden (Nya Sverige) was a Swedish colonial venture along the lower Delaware River, established when Peter Minuit led the first expedition under commission from the New Sweden Company, anchoring on 29 March 1638 to build Fort Christina at present-day Wilmington, Delaware. Settlers were predominantly Swedes and Finns — the latter eventually comprising roughly half the population — and are credited with introducing the log cabin to North America. Governor Johan Björnsson Printz (r. 1643–1653) expanded fortifications and developed a productive fur-trade relationship with the Susquehannock. Dutch Director-General Peter Stuyvesant arrived with seven ships and 317 soldiers in 1655, besieged Fort Christina until it surrendered on 15 September 1655, absorbing New Sweden into New Netherland.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The colonial territory's core along the Delaware is well documented from Swedish, Dutch, and English colonial records; claimed hinterland extent was largely nominal and contested with New Netherland from the outset.
